cases.indication: COVID-19 vaccine full biologics license; NUVAXOVID

observations.finding: Contemporaneous annual-report context describes the COVID-19 vaccine business and risks involving regulatory approval and third-party manufacturing. It is not a complete reconstruction of the BLA efficacy, safety or CMC submission.
observations.source_location: Annual report business and manufacturing/regulatory risk factors

observations.finding: An April 23 issuer statement about BLA approvability follows the legacy April 1 goal and is excluded from that reconstruction.

The issuer describes PREVENT-19 as randomized, placebo-controlled and observer-blinded, enrolling 29,949 adults at 119 US/Mexico sites and reporting 90.4% vaccine efficacy. These are historical trial results, not an FDA approval probability or complete 2025 BLA/current-strain evidence.

The UK Phase 3 discussion reports 89.7% original efficacy and 82.5% in a later six-month analysis. These estimates concern different follow-up analyses and must not be pooled or treated as interchangeable. Variant, formulation, population and exposure differences require review before comparison with the 2025 application.
FDA original license letter records May 16 approval under BL 125817/0. Its approved population and manufacturing findings are outcome evidence, not March 31 prediction inputs.

supporting_factors: A licensed/EUA vaccine development program existed before the goal; full license is a separate regulatory event.
An exact-index-dated February 28, 2023 filing provides positive historical PREVENT-19 and UK trial efficacy context before the research cutoff.
opposing_factors: Approval delay and May 16 population restrictions cannot be imported into March 31 inputs. Detailed pre-goal BLA safety, effectiveness and CMC evidence is not yet reconstructed.
Historical efficacy analyses do not establish current-strain effectiveness, adequate older-adult precision, or absence of myocarditis risk for the 2025 application.

related_precedents.name: Prior EUA versus full BLA
related_precedents.comparison: Same sponsor/product, but EUA authorization and full licensure have different evidence requirements; neither an independent prior case nor a substitute for exact cycle adjudication.

related_precedents.name: FDA June 7, 2022 NVX-CoV2373 EUA briefing — safety and subgroup context
related_precedents.comparison: FDA briefing Table 8 identifies wide older-adult efficacy uncertainty; section 10.3 discusses myocarditis concerns. Historical EUA evidence requires separate evaluation from the 2025 BLA, updated formulation and circulating variants. The original public-availability clock is not independently recovered, so this source is context only, not an admitted prediction feature.

cases.indication: Hyperphosphatemia in chronic kidney disease patients on dialysis; oxylanthanum carbonate

observations.finding: Issuer disclosed an FDA cGMP deficiency at a third-party manufacturing vendor and that labeling discussions were precluded. This was public before the June 26 research cutoff; it does not by itself establish the eventual FDA decision.

Extracted original FDA CRL pages identify NDA 218607, Reference ID 5616346 and a June 27, 2025 signature. First-page visual verification and original public availability remain incomplete. This outcome document is excluded from pre-decision SCIENCE.
observations.source_location: Extracted later pages and signature; first page unverified

observations.finding: UNI-OLC-201 enrolled 106 patients; 86 entered the safety population and 71 the evaluable maintenance population. Treatment-related maintenance discontinuation was 1/71; all adverse-event discontinuations were 5/86, including three treatment-related. Phosphate control was reported in 77/86 after titration. The study was not designed to evaluate efficacy and lacked a concurrent active comparator. The issuer comparison with Fosrenol historical discontinuation cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy.
observations.source_location: Exhibit 99.1 topline safety, tolerability, phosphate and population sections

observations.finding: A later-cycle CRL references the June 27, 2025 action; it must not replace the original cycle or enter 2025 clinical/manufacturing prediction inputs.

supporting_factors: The program had a defined NDA/goal; clinical effectiveness still requires original protocol and results reconstruction.
A June 25, 2024 issuer disclosure reports tolerability and phosphate-control findings from UNI-OLC-201 before the research cutoff.
opposing_factors: Precutoff manufacturing deficiency and halted label discussions were a concrete opposing factor to the legacy approval prediction. No calibrated probability effect is assigned.
Different enrolled, safety and evaluable populations must remain separate; a study not designed for efficacy and historical Fosrenol comparison cannot establish comparative benefit or safety.

related_precedents.name: Other phosphate binders
related_precedents.comparison: Clinical pill burden and phosphate control require comparison with existing binders; another compound or formulation does not resolve this facility deficiency. Exact independent historical action/trial comparator remains unadjudicated.

related_precedents.name: FOSRENOL NDA021468 — prior lanthanum carbonate clinical label context
related_precedents.comparison: FDA-hosted historical labeling reports short-term placebo-controlled ESRD studies and two longer open-label comparisons; the 14% adverse-event discontinuation figure comes from the longer comparative studies. UNI-OLC-201 uses different populations, exposure and design, so its maintenance treatment-related discontinuation fraction cannot be compared directly with that 14% rate. Formulation and manufacturing identity differ.

cases.indication: Fibromyalgia in adults; sublingual cyclobenzaprine TNX-102 SL / Tonmya

observations.finding: Issuer reported RESILIENT primary pain endpoint p=0.00005 and supportive prespecified secondary endpoints, with an August 15 goal. The exhibit header says March 17 while its body says March 18; SEC filing/acceptance on March 18 is the conservative availability bound.

Issuer reports positive RESILIENT (F307) and RELIEF (F304) studies but a negative RALLY (F306) primary pain result after an IDMC futility recommendation. These are within-program trial comparisons, not independent FDA decision precedents. Missing-data handling requires review.
observations.source_location: TNX-102 SL; completed RESILIENT, RALLY and RELIEF studies, pages 14–18

observations.finding: RESILIENT reported adverse-event treatment discontinuations of 6.1% versus 3.5% with placebo; one pancreatitis serious adverse event was considered possibly treatment-related. These issuer-reported findings require original safety-table and causality review.

The filing describes exposure bridging to Amrix, a proposed 505(b)(2) pathway, commercial cGMP facilities and stability data. These issuer statements are not independently inspected FDA manufacturing findings.
Original NDA 219428 approval letter and postmarketing requirements are outcome-only evidence and cannot complete historical pre-August-15 safety assessment.

supporting_factors: A positive issuer-reported pivotal result and supportive secondary outcomes were available before the research cutoff.
The March 18 annual report describes two positive studies, RELIEF and RESILIENT, within the same development program.
opposing_factors: Full protocol/SAP, failed or inconsistent prior trials, missing-data handling, discontinuations, long-term safety and manufacturing records still require adversarial review.

The same pre-cutoff filing reports negative RALLY efficacy and RESILIENT adverse-event discontinuation and pancreatitis findings; consistent efficacy, missing-data handling and safety remain unresolved independently.

related_precedents.name: Existing fibromyalgia therapies and earlier cyclobenzaprine trials
related_precedents.comparison: Compare population, pain endpoint, blinding and route/formulation rather than borrowing another therapy's approval or treating two positive trials as the full program history.

related_precedents.name: RELIEF / RALLY / RESILIENT within-program trials
related_precedents.comparison: F304 and F307 positive versus F306 negative primary result. Same program; these comparisons must not count as independent FDA decisions or program-disjoint training cases.

cases.indication: Hereditary angioedema prophylaxis age 2 to less than 12; berotralstat oral pellets

observations.finding: June 25 filing reports FDA notification June 23 of a three-month goal extension for additional final reports and formulation data. New target was December 12; notification, amendment and public filing dates are different clocks.

Issuer reported positive pediatric APeX-P interim observations and an original September 12 target. Content was observed, but the filing-index timestamp was not successfully retrieved; this dated lead remains quarantined.

The issuer quarterly report describes APeX-P as complete through its primary endpoint, with continued assessment of oral granules in children aged 2 to 11. Existing capsule approvals for patients aged 12 and older are separate. Reported symptom reductions are not a substitute for a complete pediatric clinical study report or a randomized efficacy comparison.
observations.source_location: MD&A Products and Product Candidates; Recent Developments

observations.finding: The report records a September 12 original target and June 23 notification extending the goal to December 12 after additional final reports and formulation data. August 5 is the verified SEC filing availability, not its June 30 period end or the earlier event date. A standard review extension alone does not establish approval or nonapproval.
observations.source_location: Recent Developments: ORLADEYO pediatric NDA review extension

observations.finding: Original NDA 219776 approval letter distinguishes pediatric oral pellets from parent capsules NDA 214094, and notes a June 11 major amendment. These FDA conclusions are outcome-only evidence.

supporting_factors: Issuer-reported pediatric results and established parent-product experience provide research context, subject to age/formulation differences.
An August 5 SEC filing places pediatric primary-endpoint completion and clinical-development context within the conservative research window.
opposing_factors: Formulation/final-report amendment extended review. The 2020 parent berotralstat decision already appears in legacy history; program-family leakage has not been ruled out.

Pediatric granules require their own exposure, safety and formulation evidence; older-patient capsule experience is not an independent pediatric approval case. The August filing does not validate earlier source availability.

related_precedents.name: Parent ORLADEYO capsules NDA 214094
related_precedents.comparison: Same active ingredient/program; adult/adolescent capsules and pediatric pellets NDA 219776 differ in population/formulation. Parent is correlated evidence, not an independent held-out case.

observations.finding: Issuer describes positive pivotal GRACE findings and an enriched randomized-withdrawal architecture. Full enrollment, attrition, estimand and SAP review are needed before judging the evidence.

GRADIENT between-group systolic-pressure comparison was not statistically significant despite a reported within-relacorilant reduction from baseline. Within-arm significance is not proof of superiority versus placebo. This opposing evidence predates the CRL.
Corrected January 2026 CRL preserves December 30 action date. Its detailed FDA efficacy objections must not be used to construct a pre-December-30 model feature.

supporting_factors: GRACE met the issuer-reported primary endpoint, which warrants source-specific review rather than dismissal after the known outcome.
opposing_factors: GRADIENT between-arm result and GRACE enrichment/attrition are predecision challenges. The legacy CRL override lacks a dated freeze and cannot be counted as a successful forecast.

related_precedents.comparison: Existing hypercortisolism treatment is context; relacorilant hypertension/withdrawal endpoints differ from another drug's glycemic indication. Keep ovarian-cancer relacorilant trials separate from Cushing evidence.

cases.indication: Prevention of vomiting induced by motion in adults; tradipitant / Nereus

observations.finding: Issuer distinguishes the tradipitant motion-sickness NDA with a December 30 goal from the gastroparesis NDA and associated litigation/review history. Those are not interchangeable regulatory cycles.

Issuer reported that partial-hold re-review was extended to December 5 and that NDA labeling discussions had begun. The December 30 NDA target remained unchanged. Labeling discussions alone do not establish approval.

Issuer reported that FDA lifted the partial clinical hold on protocol VP-VLY-686-3403, previously limited to 90 doses, following reclassification of motion-sickness use as acute and event-driven. The NDA remained under review with a December 30 target. Hold removal is distinct from NDA approval and does not establish unlimited-exposure safety.
observations.source_location: Exhibit 99.1 partial-hold update; supersedes November 28 pending re-review as issuer-reported status

observations.finding: FDA package contains original NDA 220152 approval letter for motion-induced vomiting in adults, Reference ID 5720300. Packaging under a 2026 directory does not establish original publication time.

supporting_factors: A defined motion-sickness application/goal existed before the research cutoff; clinical efficacy and safety tables still require original-study reconstruction.
The December 4 issuer disclosure reports removal of the partial hold before the research cutoff; it supersedes the November 28 pending re-review status.
opposing_factors: Gastroparesis results/CRL, motion-sickness partial-hold issues and later labeling/approval must remain separated by indication and publication date. Prior tradipitant staging raises a family-overlap check.
Hold removal concerned protocol exposure restrictions and acute event-driven use; it does not establish NDA approval, full efficacy or safety under other exposure patterns.

related_precedents.name: Prior tradipitant gastroparesis submission
related_precedents.comparison: Same molecule, different indication and trials. Prior negative action is a source-specific challenge and family-overlap concern, not the motion-sickness outcome or an independent comparator.
